Apple Mail.question: It also integrates with the _____ list, Calendar, Maps and other apps
Apple Mail.fact: It also integrates with the Contacts list, Calendar, Maps and other apps.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: It supported rich text formatting with images and voice messaging, and _____ emails
Apple Mail.fact: It supported rich text formatting with images and voice messaging, and MIME emails.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: In a beta version (codenamed "_____") and various other early pre-releases of Mac OS X, Mail was known as MailViewer
Apple Mail.fact: In a beta version (codenamed "Rhapsody") and various other early pre-releases of Mac OS X, Mail was called MailViewer.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: However, with the third developer release of _____ X, the application had returned to being known simply as Mail
Apple Mail.fact: When Apple began to adapt NeXTSTEP to become Mac OS X, both the operating system and the application went through various stages as it was developed. In a beta version (codenamed "Rhapsody") and various other early pre-releases of Mac OS X, Mail was called MailViewer.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: It was integrated with other Apple applications such as _____, iChat, and iCal
Apple Mail.fact: It was integrated with other Apple applications such as Address Book, iChat, and iCal.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: Additional features were: "Smart mailboxes" that used _____ technology to sort mail into folders
Apple Mail.fact: Additional features were: "Smart mailboxes" that used Spotlight technology to sort mail into folders.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: It also introduced _____ IDLE support for account inboxes
Apple Mail.fact: It also introduced IMAP IDLE support for account inboxes.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: The bounce function, where unwanted emails could be bounced back to the sender, was dropped, as was support for _____ push email
Apple Mail.fact: The bounce function, where unwanted emails could be bounced back to the sender, was dropped, as was support for Exchange push email. Streaming notification support for Exchange accounts was also added.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: Streaming notification support for _____ accounts was also added
Apple Mail.fact: The bounce function, where unwanted emails could be bounced back to the sender, was dropped, as was support for Exchange push email. Streaming notification support for Exchange accounts was also added.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: Mail now also supports interactive notifications and integrates with the _____ app to let Siri suggest possible reminders based on who you are emailing
Apple Mail.fact: Mail now also supports interactive notifications and integrates with the Reminders app to let Siri suggest possible reminders based on who you are emailing.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: Extensions from the _____ can now integrate with the Mail app, and iCloud+ subscribers can easily create a new email address that forwards to their primary address
Apple Mail.fact: Extensions from the Mac App Store can now integrate with the Mail app, and iCloud+ subscribers can easily create a new email address that forwards to their primary address.

Apple Mail.subject: Computer & IT
Apple Mail.question: Emails from companies now show their logo using _____ support
Apple Mail.fact: Emails from companies now show their logo using BIMI support.

Application layer.subject: Computer & IT
Application layer.question: What is Application layer? Highest layer in network protocol models.
Application layer.fact: An application layer is an abstraction layer that specifies the shared communication protocols and interface methods used by hosts in a communications network.   An application layer abstraction is specified in both the Internet Protocol Suite (TCP/IP) and the OSI model.

Application security.subject: Computer & IT
Application security.question: What is Application security? Measures taken to improve the security of an application.
Application security.fact: Application security (AppSec) includes all tasks that introduce a secure software development life cycle to development teams.   Web application security is a branch of information security that deals specifically with the security of websites, web applications, and web services.

Application server.subject: Computer & IT
Application server.question: What is Application server? Server that hosts applications.
Application server.fact: An application server is a server that hosts applications or software that delivers a business application through a communication protocol.   For a typical web application, the application server sits behind the web servers.

Application service provider.subject: Computer & IT
Application service provider.question: What is Application service provider? Business providing software via the web.
Application service provider.fact: An application service provider (ASP) is a business providing application software generally through the Web.

Application software.subject: Computer & IT
Application software.question: What is Application software? Any computer program for end-user use.
Application software.fact: Application software is software that is intended for end-user use – not operating, administering or programming a computer.   An application (app, application program, software application) is any program that can be categorized as application software.

Application software.subject: Computer & IT
Application software.question: The abbreviation app became popular with the _____ introduction of the iOS App Store, to refer to applications for mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets
Application software.fact: The abbreviation app became popular with the 2008 introduction of the iOS App Store, to refer to applications for mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets.

Application software.subject: Computer & IT
Application software.question: Later, with the release of the Mac App Store in _____ and the Windows Store in 2011, it began to be used to refer to end-user software in general, regardless of platform
Application software.fact: Later, with the release of the Mac App Store in 2010 and the Windows Store in 2011, it began to be used to refer to end-user software in general, regardless of platform.

Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.question: The _____ was Feature of the TLS network security protocol.
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.fact: Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) is a Transport Layer Security (TLS) extension that allows the application layer to negotiate which protocol should be performed over a secure connection in a manner that avoids additional round trips and which is independent of the application-layer protocols.

Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.question: This extension was used to negotiate experimental SPDY connections between _____ and some of Google's servers
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.fact: This extension was used to negotiate experimental SPDY connections between Google Chrome and some of Google's servers. TLS False Start was disabled in Google Chrome from version 20 (2012) onward except for websites with the earlier NPN extension.

Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.question: As _____ evolved, NPN was replaced with ALPN
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.fact: This extension was used to negotiate experimental SPDY connections between Google Chrome and some of Google's servers. As SPDY evolved, NPN was replaced with ALPN.

Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.question: ALPN replaces _____ (NPN) extension
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.fact: ALPN replaces Next Protocol Negotiation (NPN) extension.

Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.question: TLS False Start was disabled in Google Chrome from version 20 (_____) onward except for websites with the earlier NPN extension
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation.fact: TLS False Start was disabled in Google Chrome from version 20 (2012) onward except for websites with the earlier NPN extension.

Application-release automation.subject: Computer & IT
Application-release automation.question: The _____ was Process of packaging and deployment.
Application-release automation.fact: Application-release automation (ARA) refers to the process of packaging and deploying an application or update of an application from development, across various environments, and ultimately to production.

Applied science.subject: Computer & IT
Applied science.question: What is Applied science? Practical application of scientific knowledge.
Applied science.fact: Applied science is the application of the scientific method and scientific knowledge to attain practical goals.   Applied science is often contrasted with basic science, which is focused on advancing scientific theories and laws that explain and predict natural or other phenomena.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: The _____ was Pathological behavior by an apportionment rule.
Apportionment paradox.fact: An apportionment paradox is a situation where an apportionment—a rule for dividing discrete objects according to some proportional relationship—produces results that violate notions of common sense or fairness.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: However, as shown by the _____–Young theorem, it is not always possible to provide a perfectly fair resolution that satisfies all competing fairness criteria
Apportionment paradox.fact: However, as shown by the Balinski–Young theorem, it is not always possible to provide a perfectly fair resolution that satisfies all competing fairness criteria.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: An actual impact was observed in _____, when Virginia lost a seat to Maine, even though Virginia's population was growing more rapidly: this is an example of the population paradox
Apportionment paradox.fact: An actual impact was observed in 1900, when Virginia lost a seat to Maine, even though Virginia's population was growing more rapidly: this is an example of the population paradox.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: In _____, when Oklahoma became a state, New York lost a seat to Maine, thus the name "the new state paradox"
Apportionment paradox.fact: In 1907, when Oklahoma became a state, New York lost a seat to Maine, thus the name "the new state paradox".

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: In _____, when Oklahoma became a state, it was given a fair share of seats and the total number of seats increased by that number
Apportionment paradox.fact: In 1907, when Oklahoma became a state, New York lost a seat to Maine, thus the name "the new state paradox".

Apportionment paradox.question: Third, any state whose fair share is less than one receives one seat, regardless of population, as required by the _____
Apportionment paradox.fact: Third, any state whose fair share is less than one receives one seat, regardless of population, as required by the United States Constitution.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: The Hamilton method replaced a rounding method proposed by Thomas Jefferson, and was itself replaced by the Huntington–Hill method in _____
Apportionment paradox.fact: The Hamilton method replaced a rounding method proposed by Thomas Jefferson, and was itself replaced by the Huntington–Hill method in 1941.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: The US House of _____ is constitutionally required to allocate seats based on population counts, which are required every 10 years
Apportionment paradox.fact: The US House of Representatives is constitutionally required to allocate seats based on population counts, which are required every 10 years.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: The size of the _____ is set by statute
Apportionment paradox.fact: The US House of Representatives is constitutionally required to allocate seats based on population counts, which are required every 10 years. The size of the House is set by statute.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: In general the term _____ paradox refers to any apportionment scenario where increasing the total number of items would decrease one of the shares
Apportionment paradox.fact: After the 1880 census, C. W. Seaton, chief clerk of the United States Census Bureau, computed apportionments for all House sizes between 275 and 350, and discovered that Alabama would get eight seats with a House size of 299 but only seven with a House size of 300. In general the term Alabama paradox refers to any apportionment scenario where increasing the total number of items would decrease one of the shares.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
Apportionment paradox.question: Some of the earlier _____ apportionment methods, such as Hamilton, could exhibit the population paradox
Apportionment paradox.fact: Some of the earlier Congressional apportionment methods, such as Hamilton, could exhibit the population paradox.

Apportionment paradox.subject: Computer & IT
